findings.problem: status is a free-form `String` — any value is constructable including `"invalid"`, `""`, `"SENT"`, or any string that does not correspond to a legitimate lifecycle stage
findings.failure_mode: A caller can create or mutate a PacketWorkflow into an unparseable or undefined status; downstream match/if-else on status must exhaustively handle every possible UTF-8 string or risk undefined behavior
findings.fix: Replace `pub status: String` with a domain enum `PacketStatus` (e.g., `Pending`, `Validated`, `Sent`) with a `FromStr` or fallible `try_from` constructor

findings.problem: `is_validated: bool` is a primitive flag that cannot encode the invariant that validation must occur before sending
findings.failure_mode: A packet can be `is_sent=true` while `is_validated=false`, representing a violated lifecycle invariant; `mark_sent` does not check validation at all
findings.fix: Replace `is_validated: bool` with a typestate or include it as part of a single `PacketStatus` enum so that `Sent` variant inherently implies prior validation

findings.problem: `is_sent: bool` is a primitive flag that duplicates state already encoded in `status` string and can diverge from it
findings.failure_mode: Caller can set `is_sent=true` while `status` remains `"pending"`, or call `mark_sent` to set both, creating redundant and conflict-prone mutation; no single source of truth for lifecycle
findings.fix: Replace `is_sent: bool` with a single `status: PacketStatus` enum; eliminate the boolean entirely so the enum is the sole lifecycle oracle

findings.problem: `mark_sent` blindly sets `status="sent"` and `is_sent=true` without checking `is_validated`, allowing unvalidated packets to enter sent state
findings.failure_mode: Business invariant (validate-before-send) is violated at runtime with no compiler or check-level enforcement; a caller can send any packet regardless of validation state
findings.fix: Replace `mark_sent` with a fallible function `try_mark_sent(item: PacketWorkflow) -> Result<PacketWorkflow, PacketError>` that rejects non-validated packets, or bake the transition into the `PacketStatus` enum where `Sent` is only reachable from `Validated`

findings.problem: `id: String` is a raw `String` with no domain semantics — any string is a valid ID including empty or malformed values
findings.failure_mode: Callers can construct packets with empty, whitespace-only, or otherwise invalid IDs; no validation at the type boundary
findings.fix: Introduce `pub struct PacketId(String)` with a fallible `try_from(String) -> Result<PacketId, ParseError>` constructor that rejects empty/invalid IDs

findings.problem: `PacketWorkflow` contains owned `String` fields (`id`, `status`) making it heavy to copy and not borrow-friendly; the struct is a data carrier mixed with mutable behavior in `mark_sent`
findings.failure_mode: Every pass-by-value of `PacketWorkflow` allocates/copies two `String`s; the pure data is not cleanly separated from the imperative mutation in `mark_sent`
findings.fix: Use `Cow<'static, str>` or `&str` at parse boundaries for borrowed use; separate a pure `PacketStatus` data type from shell-side mutation; make `mark_sent` a pure state-transition function returning the new status rather than mutating in place

findings.problem: `status: String` and `is_sent: bool` encode overlapping lifecycle information — `is_sent` is a boolean projection of `status`, creating redundant state
findings.failure_mode: Inconsistency between `status` and `is_sent` is possible; any new boolean flag adds another point of potential divergence as the domain grows
findings.fix: Collapse to a single `PacketStatus` enum; derive `is_sent` as a method `fn is_sent(&self) -> bool` on the enum

no second-ring audit or formal typestate proof that lifecycle transitions are exhaustive
no command evidence (cargo test, cargo fmt, cargo clippy) was run or recorded
residual_risk: The struct encodes multiple independent primitive flags that can represent illegal combinations (e.g., sent without validated, empty status, divergent status/is_sent). The core domain invariants are not enforced by the type system at all — every transition is unchecked mutable mutation. Without enum-based typestates, no static analysis can guarantee valid lifecycle. Full rewrite of PacketWorkflow into a typestate enum with fallible transitions is required before any production use.
